info.description:
API for accessing video content, collections, playlists, and AI-powered features.

## Authentication

Most API endpoints require authentication via a BOLD API token. Include your token
in the `Authorization` header as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN
```

Session-management client endpoints under `/api/v1/auth/*` use the customer's
upstream IdP JWT instead:

```
Authorization: Bearer UPSTREAM_IDP_JWT
X-Bold-Tenant-Slug: YOUR_TENANT_SLUG
```

Server-side session-management integration endpoints under
`/api/v1/session-management/*` use the normal tenant BOLD API token. These
endpoints are for customer-owned servers to inspect and revoke device sessions
after the customer app has already decided the viewer is allowed to access content.

Admin endpoints under `/api/v1/admin/*` require `X-Bold-Admin-Api-Key` and are
reserved for Mission Control or deliberately privileged support automation.

## Browser CORS

Public tenant-token APIs and `/api/v1/auth/*` accept cross-origin browser
requests, including preflights, without cookie credentials. Send authorization
headers with `credentials: "omit"`; wildcard origins never allow credentials.
Admin, server-side session-management, internal and cookie-authenticated app
routes do not opt into CORS. Call privileged endpoints from your server.

MCP chat credentials can continue only their connection's viewer's library conversations;
current connection grants replace body grants, and revoked/expired credentials are refused.
Verified-access conversations require the server-only credential, resolved viewer and matching
normalized access/focus on every turn, even after disabling the tenant policy. Changed grants
or focus return 409 ai_access_scope_changed; start a new conversation. current_time may change.
Send focus on each turn to select a video, change it, or omit it to return
to library chat. Focus answers and widened answers share this conversation;
scope is returned on message_complete, JSON, and assistant history.
Repeat access lists on every turn; they are never reused from a previous request.
Access has the same empty-list, confidence, pointers and locked-match semantics
as the initial chat request. synthesize=false skips focus answering and both probes.
Video sources include a fresh playback_token for signed playback; public and non-playback sources use null.

The AI maintains context from previous messages in the conversation.
JSON and `message_complete` include `interaction_id` and the persisted assistant
`message_id` for feedback on answers and clarifications. Reuse a UUID `request_id`
for retries of the same turn. This deduplicates best-effort asynchronous
analytics, not model execution or responses.
Optional channel/client metadata is outside retry identity; invalid values are
recorded as unknown and never reject the request.
Error responses omit internal provider and exception details.
Answer responses include public-safe retrieval metadata: `retrieval_mode`, `degraded`,
and `degraded_reason`.

When `synthesize` is false, successful retrieval returns ordered uncited evidence with
`response_type: "retrieval"`. SSE uses one terminal `message_complete` event carrying that
retrieval result. Query planning can still return a clarification response before retrieval.

Answers are finalized the same way as "Chat with your video library": claims
carrying unknown citation markers are removed, exact cited video titles become
Markdown links, and the terminal `answer` event is authoritative over
concatenated `text_delta` chunks.

post.description:
Returns 403 verified_ai_route_unsupported when verified AI access is required.
Existing voice sessions are not cancelled by this policy; operators must stop them before enabling it.
Starts a real-time spoken conversation about one accessible, published video, grounded in its transcript.

Existing credentials access public videos only. Private published lessons require
a separately issued server-only key with private_video_ai permission and a customer
server entitlement check. Viewer IDs do not grant access. Unlisted, unpublished
and non-ready videos return 404 for every credential, matching text chat.

Send the browser's WebRTC SDP offer and apply the returned `sdp` answer as the
peer connection's remote description. Bold chooses the model, voice, and
instructions, and the browser's data channel is limited to mute, unmute,
context appends, and close. End the call client-side after `max_seconds`, or
after `idle_seconds` of silence.

Voice must also be enabled in the account's AI Settings. Turning it off
refuses new sessions with `403 feature_disabled`. Voice, persona and limits
are resolved when a session starts; changes do not affect a running session.

The complete instructions have a 54,000-character budget, including personality,
viewer context and grounding rules. Transcripts that exceed the remaining space
are sampled evenly across the whole video so the session can still name late moments.

Each account has a voice-minute allowance for the UTC calendar month. Once it is
used up, new sessions are refused with `402 voice_allowance_exceeded` and the
day the allowance resets; sessions already running are unaffected.
Open calls reserve their full maximum duration. The last admitted call may
exceed the remaining allowance; this is not an exact spending ceiling.

A viewer holds one session at a time. Starting a second one for the same
viewer is refused with `409 voice_session_limit`; end the first session, or
wait for it to end on its own, before starting another.
Omitted viewers share one anonymous slot per account. Unconfirmed shutdowns
retain their slot and reservation until cleanup succeeds.

post.description:
Ask questions across your entire video library.
When Require verified AI access is enabled, a fresh server-only verified_ai_access key,
resolved viewer and explicit access object are required. Viewer IDs are not entitlement proof;
the customer server must authorize every grant and focus. Empty access is focus-only/no library.
Conversations bind normalized grants and focus ID. Changed scope or unbound history returns
409 ai_access_scope_changed: start a new conversation. Bound history stays protected after
disabling the policy. Admission errors are JSON before SSE starts. No cross-conversation memory
is supplied to bound conversations. Existing streams may finish after policy changes.
MCP chat credentials are accepted on this POST route and its POST continuation only.
Their connection supplies viewer and answer/point grants; body viewer, access, collection
filters and inline profile cannot override them. Mention is empty and focus is refused.
Private lessons additionally require the approving key's private-video capability.
MCP turns retain synced viewer traits and this conversation's history, but receive no
shared viewer memory or summaries of other conversations.
Send `focus: {video_id, current_time?}` to read that video first, then search
this same library pipeline on a miss, without clarification. Focus is per turn;
omit it to drop focus. Video access uses the same credential gate as video chat.
Focused responses include `scope` in JSON, message_complete, and stored history.
Focus SSE adds reading/widening progress and one scope event before text.
With synthesize=false, focus is authorized but its LLM step is skipped.
Optional `access` supplies per-turn answer/point/mention collection lists.
It is the caller's assertion, not verified viewer entitlement. Missing lists
mean empty; empty answer skips library search, expansion and manifest loading.
Access overrides collection_ids and disables resource retrieval. Only answer
collections enter library prompts. Empty candidates or low confidence fall through to
data-only point/mention probes. Pointers and locked_matches follow text and
precede message_complete; the same arrays persist in history and JSON.
With synthesize=false, only answer-list evidence is returned; probes are skipped.
Conversation creation failures return a processing_failed JSON error before
streaming starts, including when stream=true.
Video sources include a fresh playback_token for signed playback; public and non-playback sources use null.

The AI searches all transcripts, finds relevant content, and synthesizes an answer with citations.
Collection filters also restrict the library structure supplied to the AI prompts.
Factual name lookups use exact lexical recovery across profiles and transcripts. If factual
retrieval is empty or weak, the response describes what the search could not find rather than asserting absence.
Use `conversation_id` from the response to ask follow-up questions.
JSON and `message_complete` include a turn-specific `interaction_id`.
Reuse a UUID `request_id` on retries for analytics deduplication, not response replay.
Capture is best-effort and asynchronous; the ID is not a persistence acknowledgement.
Answers and clarifications also include the persisted assistant `message_id` for feedback.
Optional `channel`, `client_name`, and `client_version` are analytics metadata,
outside retry identity. Invalid metadata becomes unknown and never rejects AI.
Error responses omit internal provider and exception details.

Set `synthesize=false` to stop after retrieval and return ordered evidence with
`response_type: "retrieval"`. This mode persists the user query but no assistant
answer. Evidence IDs are deterministic within the ranked response, not durable
database IDs. Callers that synthesize answers elsewhere must send standalone
follow-up prompts because those external answers are not part of Bold's history.

**Streaming (default):** Returns SSE events:
- `message_start`: Stream started
- `conversation_created`: Conversation record created
- `image_analysis`: Uploaded images analyzed
- `progress`: Pipeline stage status (e.g. "Searching your library…")
- `sources`: Search results found
- `citation_map`: Stable citation map for streamed text
- `text_delta`: Raw answer text chunk (pre-finalization, see below)
- `answer`: Complete finalized answer with citations and public-safe retrieval metadata
- `message_complete`: Stream finished (carries the same finalized `content`)

With `synthesize=false`, `message_complete` is the only terminal success event.
It contains `response_type: "retrieval"`, `sources`, `confidence`, and retrieval
`metadata`; it omits answer content, citations, and synthesis usage.

**Answer finalization:** `text_delta` events stream raw model tokens. The final
answer text is then validated: any marker-delimited claim carrying an unknown
citation marker is removed (fail closed), and exact titles of cited videos are
rewritten as Markdown links to the video's canonical portal URL. The terminal `answer` event
(and `message_complete.content`) carry this finalized text — it is authoritative
and is what gets persisted to the conversation. Clients MUST replace their
accumulated `text_delta` buffer with `answer.content` on receipt; the finalized
text can differ from the concatenated deltas.

Answer responses include public-safe retrieval metadata: `retrieval_mode`, `degraded`,
and `degraded_reason`. When retrieval recovers after Stage 1 exhaustion,
`retrieval_mode` is `degraded` and `degraded_reason` is `stage1_exhausted`.

Set `stream=false` for a single JSON response whose `content` is the same
finalized answer text, with the same retrieval metadata.

patch.description:
The comment-shaped mirror of the post repair route: corrects a comment's
`content`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. The author, the thread the
comment belongs to, the counters, and `external_ref` are untouched, even if
the request body carries them. Comments have no `category`.

As on posts, replaying a `POST` with a known `external_ref` is a pure read,
so this `PATCH` is the only way to correct an imported comment; and an
update that does not carry `updated_at` stamps it to now.

Never notifies, same as everything else on this surface.
Deleted comment placeholders cannot be repaired and return 404.

Corrects a post's `content`, `category`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. The
author, the counters, and `external_ref` are untouched, even if the request
body carries them.

This is a **different verb** from `external_ref` replay: replaying a
`POST` with a known `external_ref` stays a pure read of the stored row.
This `PATCH` is the only way to correct a botched import without deleting
and re-importing the post — and a corrected `created_at` moves the post to
its right place in the feed.

Omitted fields keep their stored values, with one Ecto-level exception: as
on any edit, an update that does not carry `updated_at` stamps it to now.
Send `updated_at` alongside `created_at` when repairing the dates of a row
that was never really edited.

Never notifies, same as post/comment creation on this surface.
